title: Schotter drift
label: A lattice of squares where order and disorder trade places in drifting patches, some squares opening into nested ones, while slow rings of order cross the sheet.

title: Ruled disorder
label: Bands of short strokes slide past one another, each band drifting between one strict direction and a mix of verticals and diagonals, while a travelling gap parts the strokes around a moving point.

title: Trames moire
label: Two sets of fine concentric rings with slightly shifted centres overprint inside a disc; the interference pattern sweeps across as the two centres circle in opposite directions.

title: Tesseract
label: A hypercube turning in four dimensions, projected to a fan of fine lines where only a seeded subset of its edges is drawn.

title: Hairline flow
label: Thousands of fine hairlines combed along a slowly drifting flow field that bends around an empty disc.

title: Ribbon sheaf
label: One looping curve copied a few hundred times, each copy turned slightly further, so the hairlines build a folded translucent ribbon.

title: Iso-bands
label: Evenly spaced contour lines of a slowly drifting warped field, splitting and merging like the bands of a topographic map.

title: Glyph tiling
label: A sheet of square tiles each holding quarter-curve ribbons of hairlines that meet across the edges, sliding slowly; different rules set the tile directions in different regions, the curves straighten into diamonds around a wandering point, and slow fronts half-turn some tiles.

title: Pegs and string
math: chord from peg i to peg (k * i) mod N for every peg i; k sweeps continuously from 2 up to 2 + range and back, lingering near whole numbers (cardioid at 2, nephroid at 3, then 3, 4 and 5 cusps)
label: Pegs on a ring, each joined by a straight thin string to the peg at k times its number, while k sweeps slowly so the glowing envelope curves (cardioid, nephroid and more) bloom and fold into one another.

title: Metamorphosis
label: A sheet of hatched and empty tiles that interlock without gaps and drift sideways; their edge curves change from one shape family to another as they cross the page.

title: Harmonograph
math: x(u) = Σ A_i sin(f_i u + φ_i) m_i(u), y(u) likewise; f_i = a_i N + e_i integers, m_i(u) = 0.55 + 0.45 cos(k_i u + ψ_i), u in [0, 2π]
label: One closed pen path from four pendulums with near-integer frequency ratios; a periodic amplitude envelope winds the spiral in and out and the ink gathers where the path retraces.

title: Clifford attractor
math: x' = sin(a y) + c cos(a x),  y' = sin(b x) + d cos(b y);  (a, b) walk a small circle
label: A swarm of particles hopping along a Clifford attractor, each leaving a short comet trail, while the map parameters walk a small circle so the filigree unfolds and refolds; a second, smaller attractor streams beside it.

title: Epicycles
math: z(s) = Σ c_k e^(i k s), twelve integer k, |c_k| ~ 1/|k|^1.2
label: A field of epicycle machines of many sizes: each chain of turning circles draws its own closed curve, and the circles slowly swell and fade so the curves keep changing.

title: Chladni figure
math: u = cos t (cos n pi x cos m pi y - cos m pi x cos n pi y) + sin t (same with n', m');  sand on u = 0, contours at u = +-0.15, +-0.3
label: The standing-wave pattern of a square plate drawn as contours of the displacement, with sand collecting on the lines where the plate stays still while two vibration modes cross-fade.

title: Phyllotaxis
math: r = c sqrt(n),  phi = n (137.5078 deg + delta),  delta wanders by a few hundredths of a degree
label: One sunflower of halftone dots whose divergence angle drifts a hair around the golden angle, so the spiral arms sweep, merge and change count, with a faint echo of itself that makes a moire halo.

title: Hyperbolic tiling
math: {p,q} tiling of the Poincare disc; geodesics are circle arcs orthogonal to |z|=1; z -> (z + a)/(1 + conj(a) z), a(theta) a closed orbit
label: A regular tiling of the hyperbolic plane drawn in the Poincare disc: pentagons and heptagons shrink toward the rim while a moving Mobius shift makes the whole tiling swim like a fisheye.

title: Apollonian gasket
math: k4 = k1 + k2 + k3 +- 2 sqrt(k1k2 + k2k3 + k3k1); circles move by z -> (z - a)/(1 - conj(a) z), a(theta) a closed orbit
label: An Apollonian gasket, the packing of tangent circles generated by Descartes' theorem, swirled by a Mobius map that carries every circle to another exact circle and keeps all tangencies.

title: Penrose phason drift
math: x.e_j + g_j in Z, e_j = (cos 2pi j/5, sin 2pi j/5), sum g_j = 0; rhomb vertices sum_m K_m e_m, K_m = ceil(x.e_m + g_m); g_j = g0_j + A cos(theta + 4 pi j/5)
label: A Penrose rhomb tiling generated from a pentagrid whose lines slowly slide, so tiles flip in place while the pattern stays a perfect Penrose tiling.

title: Roulette rosette
math: x = (R-r) cos u + d cos(((R-r)/r) u), y = (R-r) sin u - d sin(((R-r)/r) u), R/r = a/b rational; d stepped per copy
label: A hypotrochoid drawn ninety times, each copy with the pen offset a little larger and the copy turned a little further, so the copies weave moire rosettes.

title: Liggende acht
math: x = sin(a t + phi), y = sin(b t), a:b = 1:1, 1:2, 2:3, 3:4; neighbours blended coefficient by coefficient so the curve stays closed; ribbon = 3 copies offset by d along the normal, over/under alternating at the 2ab-a-b crossings
label: The lying eight opens into a double loop, then a triple-loop knot and back: one closed Lissajous line drawn as a ribbon of three pencils that passes over and under itself at every crossing.

title: Knoop
math: x = (R + r cos qt) cos pt,  y = (R + r cos qt) sin pt,  z = r sin qt  (torus knot T(p,q); the trefoil is T(2,3))
label: A torus knot drawn as a ribbon of three pencil lines turns slowly in space and melts from the trefoil into five-crossing and larger knots, with every crossing cut so the nearer strand passes over.

title: Ritme
math: x = t - a sin t, y = -a cos t; a = 0 line, a < 1 wave, a = 1 cusp, a > 1 loops (self-crossing at t = +-t*, t* = a sin t*); a grows by row from 0 to 1.8
label: Rows of one curve, the trochoid, drawn as three-pencil ribbons: a straight line at the top turns into a wave, then a cusp, then loops that tighten row by row, and the whole sheet slowly breathes and flows.

title: Vlecht
math: strand k: angle t, radius R + r sin(m(t + 2πk/n) + φ), n strands; over where dρ/dt is larger
label: Strands in coloured pencil plait themselves round a ring; the waves drift between two numbers of humps, so the weave keeps changing its pattern while every crossing is cut with the nearer strand over.

title: Roos
math: r = cos(k t), t in [0, 4 pi), k = p/q in {5/2, 4}, blended in polar form r = (1-L) r_a + L r_b; copy j: scale 1 - j h, turn j d, petal exponent 1 + j/20
label: One rose r = cos(kt) drawn as twelve nested pencil copies that fan out like a shaded lotus, while k slides between rational values.

title: Rhombenring
math: tile(a,b) = s u_a + t u_b, u_k = (cos(pi k/n), sin(pi k/n)); ring = Z(2,...,2) minus a centred hole; tone = Lambert shade of the lifted facet E_a x E_b
label: A ring of rhombi hatched in three pencil tones by tile orientation so it reads as a twisted band; the tones turn round it and hexagons of three tiles flip.
